deliverables.title: Required deliverables presence
deliverables.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the paper present as a rendered PDF at proposal/report.pdf?

yes.criteria: proposal/report.pdf opens with text content.

no.criteria: File missing, empty, or fails to render.

leaves.question: Is a time-stamped proposal/analysis_plan.md present?

yes.criteria: analysis_plan.md exists with the model family and comparison protocol.

no.criteria: File absent.

leaves.question: Is a non-trivial logs directory present?

yes.criteria: proposal/logs/ contains fit/comparison/diagnostic logs.

no.criteria: Directory absent or empty.

leaves.question: Is the code directory present?

yes.criteria: proposal/code/ has the analysis pipeline.

no.criteria: Directory absent or non-functional.

leaves.question: Is the main results table present with the required rows?

tiers.name: all_rows
tiers.description: Table present with all required rows.
tiers.criteria: Table tab:main_results has the gray replication, M0/M1/M2 held-out, each M3 panel basis held-out, M2-vs-M1, M2-vs-best-M3 (cone-alignment headline, naming the best control), identifiability, and confound rows.

tiers.name: some_missing
tiers.description: Table present but missing some required rows.
tiers.criteria: Table exists but omits one or more required rows.

tiers.name: absent
tiers.criteria: No main results table.

leaves.question: Is the rendered PDF free of gross formatting failures?

yes.criteria: No overflowing equations, cut-off figures, or broken tables.

no.criteria: Equations overflow, figures cut off, or tables broken.

cone_conversion.title: Cone-space conversion and normalization validity
cone_conversion.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the reference white for the CIELAB/XYZ step stated?

yes.criteria: The reference white (e.g., D65) is documented.

no.criteria: No reference white documented.

leaves.question: Is the LMS normalization convention stated and justified?

yes.criteria: The LMS normalization (e.g., energy-normalized CIE 2006, von-Kries to the reference white) is stated and justified.

no.criteria: No LMS normalization convention is documented, leaving per-cone scalings ill-defined.

leaves.question: Is the cone-space conversion present, correct, and verified against the provided CIE 2006 fundamentals?

tiers.name: correct_and_verified
tiers.criteria: Uses provided CIE 2006 fundamentals via a documented path; verified on the white point and at least one chromatic reference.

tiers.name: plausible_unverified
tiers.criteria: Uses the provided fundamentals but verification is incomplete (e.g., white point only).

tiers.name: incorrect_or_undocumented
tiers.criteria: Conversion is missing, wrong, or cannot be traced to the provided fundamentals.

gray_replication.title: Gray-axis DR replication (anchor)
gray_replication.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the pipeline reproduce the 2022 gray-axis DR finding (M1 over M0)?

tiers.name: reproduced_clearly
tiers.criteria: M1 beats M0 on held-out gray data with CIs excluding no-effect.

tiers.name: weak_or_partial
tiers.criteria: Direction correct but marginal or wide CIs.

tiers.name: not_reproduced
tiers.criteria: M1 does not beat M0, contradicting the 2022 finding.

tiers.name: not_reported
tiers.criteria: No usable gray replication outcome.

leaves.question: Is the fitted gray scaling magnitude compared to the 2022 report?

yes.criteria: The fitted scaling shape/magnitude is compared quantitatively to the 2022 reported values.

no.criteria: Only the sign of M1-vs-M0 is reported, not a magnitude comparison.

leaves.question: Is a suprathreshold perceptual scale used for the anchor?

yes.criteria: The gray anchor uses an MLDS/Thurstonian suprathreshold scale, not threshold data.

no.criteria: Relies on threshold/JND data unsuited to a DR test.

model_comparison.title: Model family and comparison rigor
model_comparison.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Are M0, M1, M2, and the full M3 non-cone control panel (opponent, sRGB, CIE RGB, CIELAB, CIE HCL) all fit?

yes.description: M0, M1, M2 and the whole M3 panel fit.
yes.criteria: Logs contain fits for M0, M1, M2, and every required M3 panel basis (opponent, sRGB, CIE RGB, CIELAB, CIE HCL) on the same folds.

no.criteria: One or more of M0/M1/M2, or any required M3 panel basis, is missing.

leaves.question: Is the comparison evaluated on held-out data?

yes.criteria: Models compared by cross-validated held-out likelihood/error.

no.criteria: In-sample only or absent.

leaves.question: Does the comparison account for M2's extra parameters?

tiers.name: held_out_or_penalized
tiers.criteria: M2's advantage is judged on held-out data and/or a penalized criterion at matched folds.

tiers.name: not_clear
tiers.criteria: Ambiguous whether extra parameters are controlled.

tiers.name: in_sample_only
tiers.criteria: M2 favored by in-sample fit without penalty or held-out evaluation.

leaves.question: Does M2 fit genuinely distinct per-cone scalings (not a degenerate collapse to M1)?

tiers.name: genuine
tiers.criteria: M2 estimates distinct per-cone scalings, evidenced in logs.

tiers.name: not_assessable
tiers.criteria: Cannot tell from logs whether M2 is genuinely per-cone.

tiers.name: degenerate_collapse
tiers.criteria: M2 collapses to M1 (equal/degenerate per-cone functions); no genuine per-cone test.

leaves.question: Is the M3 non-cone control a panel of fixed, scale-matched bases (opponent, sRGB, CIE RGB, CIELAB, CIE HCL) of matched parameter count?

yes.criteria: M3 is a panel of the required fixed non-cone bases (opponent, sRGB, CIE RGB, CIELAB, CIE HCL) -- none a fitted free rotation -- each of the same parameter count as M2, with axes scaled/whitened comparably to the cone axes. For the perceptually-defined spaces (CIELAB, CIE HCL), the control uses a fixed, disclosed transform on its own coordinate differences, NOT a per-stimulus or data-adaptive linearization.

no.description: M3 panel missing, incomplete, or not matched.
no.criteria: M3 is a fitted free rotation, only a single control, missing one or more of the required standard bases, of different complexity, or not scale-matched -- invalidating the M2-vs-best-M3 comparison. A per-stimulus/tuned linearization of CIELAB or CIE HCL (spatially-varying frame) also fails: it is data-adaptive flexibility, not a fixed matched control.

core_result.title: Core result: channel-organization and cone-alignment verdict
core_result.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is cone-alignment (M2 vs the best member of the M3 non-cone panel), not just anisotropy, tested?

yes.criteria: M2 is compared against the best-performing member of the matched non-cone control panel (opponent, sRGB, CIE RGB, CIELAB, CIE HCL) on held-out data.

no.criteria: Only M2-vs-M1 (anisotropy) is examined, or M2 is compared only against a single/weakest control rather than the best of the required panel.

leaves.question: What scientific conclusion can the held-out comparison support, after accounting for control complexity and uncertainty? Either a well-supported positive or negative result can satisfy the task; lack of power is not dishonesty.

tiers.name: supported_conclusion
tiers.description: The held-out evidence supports the positive, negative, or appropriately qualified scientific conclusion under the task's required tests.

tiers.name: underpowered_or_inconclusive
tiers.description: The performed comparison is too weak or uncertain to resolve the question at the required level.

tiers.name: not_reported
tiers.description: The necessary held-out comparison/conclusion is absent.

leaves.question: Is the headline verdict stated with uncertainty?

yes.criteria: The M2-vs-M3 (and M2-vs-M1) headline reports a 95% CI.

no.criteria: Headline stated as a point value.

identifiability.title: Identifiability, gauge, and earned nulls
identifiability.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is an identifiability analysis present?

yes.criteria: The submission analyzes what granularity of cone structure the data can resolve.

no.criteria: Identifiability not addressed.

leaves.question: Is the outer/inner (f vs f_c) gauge fixed and disclosed?

yes.criteria: A gauge convention (e.g., f(0)=0, f'(0)=1, fixed f_c reference scale) is stated, making M2 identifiable.

no.criteria: No gauge convention; the f-vs-f_c confound leaves M2 unidentifiable.

leaves.question: Is the delta-L/delta-M cone-difference collinearity quantified?

yes.criteria: A collinearity/condition diagnostic of the cone-difference design is reported.

no.criteria: No collinearity diagnostic.

leaves.question: Is per-cone recoverability established by synthetic parameter recovery?

tiers.name: rigorous
tiers.criteria: Synthetic parameter recovery quantifies what is and is not recoverable (including the cone-vs-opponent M2-vs-M3 discrimination), with CI-width analysis.

tiers.name: partial
tiers.criteria: Some recovery evidence but incomplete.

tiers.name: absent
tiers.criteria: No synthetic recovery; identifiability asserted without it.

leaves.question: Is a powered comparison run at the granularity the data supports?

yes.criteria: A powered held-out comparison at the resolvable granularity is run against M1 AND a matched non-cone control at that granularity, and its power is characterized. A documented negative/underpowered outcome (the coarse control is provably non-discriminable) satisfies this as fully as a positive one; what matters is that the power is characterized, not that the result is positive.

no.criteria: No powered comparison at the resolvable granularity; any null is a bare assertion.

leaves.question: Is the cone-vs-control (M2-vs-M3) discrimination power assessed?

yes.criteria: The submission shows whether M3-generated data can be distinguished from M2-generated data at the sampled directions (the cone-vs-opponent rotation in the L~M subspace), and reports the M2-vs-M3 delta as stable across, or explicitly conditioned on, the stated LMS normalization, so a verdict is not a fit or normalization artifact.

no.criteria: No check that the cone-vs-opponent discrimination is powered at the available directions.

confound_control.title: Hue-curvature confound control
confound_control.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the hue-curvature confound addressed?

yes.criteria: DR is explicitly separated from chord-vs-arc curvature geometry.

no.criteria: Chromatic subadditivity reported without addressing curvature.

leaves.question: How rigorously, and by the data-type-appropriate method, is the confound controlled?

tiers.name: rigorous_control
tiers.criteria: Triad/gray: near-collinear-triple restriction; pairwise: arc-vs-chord model vs an additive-metric curvature baseline; verdict shown before and after.

tiers.name: mentioned_not_controlled
tiers.criteria: Acknowledged in prose without a concrete, appropriate control.

tiers.name: absent
tiers.criteria: Neither controlled nor acknowledged.

leaves.question: Is the DR/cone verdict reported before and after the control?

yes.criteria: The verdict is shown both before and after the curvature control, demonstrating survival.

no.criteria: No before/after comparison; survival of the effect is not demonstrated.

statistical_rigor.title: Statistical rigor
statistical_rigor.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Are CIs present for inferential quantities?

yes.criteria: Model-comparison deltas and scaling parameters carry 95% CIs.

no.criteria: Inferential quantities lack uncertainty.

leaves.question: Is a documented K-fold CV protocol used?

yes.criteria: A documented (participant/triad/pair-disjoint) K-fold protocol is used.

no.criteria: No documented CV protocol.

leaves.question: Is the bootstrap/posterior UQ procedure documented?

yes.criteria: Bootstrap or posterior sampling is documented with seeds.

no.criteria: No documented resampling/posterior procedure.

leaves.question: Is across-fold variation reported?

yes.criteria: Per-fold spread or SD is reported.

no.criteria: Only aggregate metrics.

novelty_positioning.title: Novelty and positioning
novelty_positioning.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is a Related Work section present?

yes.criteria: A Related Work section exists.

no.criteria: No Related Work section.

leaves.question: Does the paper engage with the 2025 follow-ups?

tiers.name: engages_substantively
tiers.criteria: Discusses Now in Color and the CGF geometry paper and their relationship to this work.

tiers.name: citation_only
tiers.criteria: Cited but not discussed.

tiers.name: only_2022_cited
tiers.criteria: 2025 follow-ups absent.

tiers.name: not_present
tiers.criteria: No prior-work engagement.

leaves.question: Is the contribution distinct (cone-alignment, not restated prior work or mere anisotropy)?

tiers.name: clearly_distinct
tiers.criteria: Cone-alignment (M2 vs M3) is explicitly differentiated from prior DR/non-constancy and from mere anisotropy.

tiers.name: mere_anisotropy
tiers.criteria: Frames M2>M1 anisotropy as the novelty without the M2-vs-M3 cone-alignment distinction.

tiers.name: partially_overlapping
tiers.criteria: Some framing overlaps prior work without clear differentiation.

tiers.name: restates_prior_result
tiers.criteria: Presents chromatic DR / non-constancy / the geometry as its own contribution.

leaves.question: Is the significance of cone-alignment argued, and is that argument calibrated to the earned result?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex (Introduction / Discussion), cross-checked against the final verdict

tiers.name: argued_and_calibrated
tiers.description: Significance argued and scaled to the verdict.
tiers.criteria: The paper makes an explicit significance argument (compact prediction of the whole space from few experiments; the pre-combination vs post-aggregation mechanism reading; what a non-cone match would imply) AND scales the mechanism/biology claims to what the earned verdict supports (a null/coarse/underpowered outcome is not dressed up as an established mechanism).

tiers.name: argued_but_overstated
tiers.description: Significance argued but overstated relative to the result.
tiers.criteria: A significance/mechanism narrative is present but asserts more than the earned verdict supports (e.g. a strong biological-mechanism claim attached to a null, coarse-only, or underpowered result).

tiers.name: not_argued
tiers.criteria: The paper reports the model comparison without arguing its scientific importance.

data_provenance.title: Data provenance and observation models
data_provenance.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Are datasets cited with sources and licenses?

yes.criteria: Each dataset cited with source and license.

no.criteria: Sources or licenses missing.

leaves.question: Are per-dataset observation models used instead of naive scale pooling?

yes.criteria: Differing response scales use per-dataset observation models (2AFC/MLDS/dissimilarity) with shared latent scalings or meta-analytic combination.

no.criteria: Incompatible response scales are pooled into one likelihood without per-dataset observation models.

failure_analysis.title: Failure analysis
failure_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

yes.criteria: The paper analyzes where its analysis fails or cannot conclude.

no.criteria: No failure analysis.

leaves.question: How specific is the failure analysis?

tiers.criteria: Identifies concrete regimes/specifications that could not be fit or identified, with evidence.

writing_quality.title: Writing quality
writing_quality.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is substantive contract content in the main paper (not dumped in the appendix)?

yes.criteria: Model comparison, identifiability, and confound content are in the main body.

no.criteria: Main paper is a skeleton with substance in the appendix.

leaves.question: Is an explicit, substantive limitations discussion present and adequate for evaluating the work's scientific scope? Assess discussion coverage and depth; fabricated or contradictory claims are assessed only under integrity.

tiers.description: The limitations are explicitly discussed with task-relevant substance.

leaves.question: Is the paper free of task-spec vocabulary?

yes.criteria: No spec-only vocabulary (e.g., 'the contract', 'held fixed', 'reward hacking', 'the four principles'). Model names like M0/M1/M2/M3 are legitimate scientific notation and are not spec leakage.

no.criteria: Task-spec-only phrasing appears in the paper.

leaves.question: Are figures and tables journal quality?

yes.criteria: Figures/tables have labels, units, CIs, and captions.

no.criteria: Figures/tables miss labels, units, CIs, or captions.

assessment_policy.scope: Completeness and scientific quality only: required artifacts, executed experimental coverage, reproducible methodology, mathematical/statistical validity, performance targets, and task-required analysis/writing.
assessment_policy.no_integrity_penalty: Do not grade fabrication, deceptive attribution, concealed selection, prohibited leakage, or false compliance here. Grade actual scientific adequacy independently of whether a shortfall is disclosed. Integrity evidence is assessed only in integrity_check_rubric.json.
assessment_policy.authoritative_task: The accompanying unchanged task specification controls required versus optional work and permitted exceptions. A qualitative quality tier is not authority to introduce a new experiment, resource limit, or numerical minimum absent from the task.
assessment_policy.conditional_nodes: Respect applicability. Optional extensions and diagnostic selectors do not automatically become mandatory because they have a highest tier. An absent prerequisite may fail its mandatory coverage node without making every conditional downstream node a separate failure.
assessment_policy.inference: Insufficient scientific support is not itself dishonesty. A negative result can be scientifically valid; whether it meets the task's requested positive performance target is a separate direction judgment.
